name: Agustin N. Coppari Hollmann
headline: ML Compiler Research @ UC Berkeley | EECS @ TUM | CDTM | Co-founder of neuroTUM e.V., LATUM and OpenHardware Initiative | Won the AMD Open Hardware 2025
location: United States, United States of America
summary:
I am an Electrical Engineering student from Argentina and a Visiting Researcher at UC Berkeley’s SLICE Lab, where I develop MLIR and IREE compiler infrastructure for custom RISC-V targets. My work focuses on the Merlin lowering pipeline and domain-specific optimizations for AI acceleration.

As a student at TUM and CDTM, I’ve co-founded neuroTUM, LATUM, and the OpenHardware Initiative to bridge the gap between high-level AI research and specialized hardware. I am passionate about HW/SW co-design, specifically in the context of neuromorphic computing and mixed-signal design.

positions.description: neuroTUM is a group of students interested in neuroscience and engineering. Our intention is to share our enthusiasm about neuroengineering and make this interdisciplinary research area more accessible. Together, we are collecting hands-on-experience by developing a brain-computer-interface (BCI) system to non-invasively decode electrical signals into precise control commands using Deep Learning architectures.

positions.title: Student Mentor
positions.description: Adveisor is the soft skill program for electrical engineers at the TUM. The program focuses on students, which want to gain more experiences within their academic career and choose to grow with challenges. The aim is to train young students in more than just their field of study - to evolve into engineers who understand themselves and those around them, who can inspire and animate their peers. The concept behind this is a trinity of knowledge, methodology and personal experience, to be gained and tested by working in teams on an engineering project.
